from the mid-2020s that is characterized by a blue-pink-yellow color palette, chaotic pattern mixing and layering, unconventional, often revealing styling choices, and music-themed visual elements. Candy Sleaze draws inspiration from 2010s fashion aesthetics such as
, incorporating and remixing elements from these trends to create a style that feels fresh, edgy, and subversive.

The term "Candy Sleaze" is a reference to the aesthetics' styling habits: "candy" refers to the bright pastel color palette, whereas "sleaze" refers to the sexy, "sleazy" nature of the outfits within the style. As this is a wiki-coined term, most examples of this style will not be labelled as
outside of this page, but many do contain references to candy in some capacity.

Visually, the aesthetic is defined by the aforementioned color palette, as well as by the usage of bright pastels, music-themed elements, layered accessories, and a few key fashion staples -- namely, bright-colored wigs, polka dot and stripe patterns, musical graphics such as staff notes and MP3 player/iPod mockups, and high heels over knee socks.

The formation of Candy Sleaze is the result of several high-profile influences combined with the natural reappearance of 2010s trends due to the fashion trend cycle. In 2025, polka dots had a major resurgence, with online publications such as CR Fashion Book and CNN noting its appearance in celebrity fashion and on the runway. Then, singer Addison Rae entered her "Headphones On era," which involved her wearing bright pink wigs, exposed underwear, and contrasting clothing sets as promotional material for her single, "Headphones On." That following fall, Japanese pop girl group f5ve released the music video to their song "I Choose You," which prominently featured the Candy Sleaze-type outfits and became the basis of the style. In their Spring/Summer 2025 collection titled "Static Fever," the brand Pixie Rebels (alongside designer Norgira) released their popular iPod Print Mini Skirt, now a staple of this trend seen in many Candy Sleaze outfit stylings and hauls. The bold color choices and styling techniques (bright tights beneath mini skirts and shorts, wigs, exposed under garments, connection with music, etc.) lended themselves well to becoming a new "It girl"/influencer style because of their uniqueness.

On April 11th, 2026, beauty news writer Sophie Vilensky published the online article "This Ultra-Nostalgic Color Combo is Literally Everywhere This Spring" for Byrdie, highlighting the teal-and-pink trend that was rising on social media platforms like TikTok. In the article, she describes the color combination as feeling "nostalgic." During the spring and summer of 2026, Candy Sleaze saw a boom in online attention. Several internet-and Instagram-focused brands had Candy Sleaze themed photoshoots to promote their products, alongside a slew of online model/influencer photoshoots: Nouviella promoted a Candy Sleaze swimwear line in April; also in April, online model Damola (@damoxla) paired up with stylist Teja Kiala (@bykiala) for the "Playing Dress Up" shoot, in which Damola wore pink, blue, and yellow garments, including cut-out tights, a sheer lace corset top, chunky jewelry, and high heels; in June, Instagram stylists Lydia Farrington (@lydialadyfarringt0n) and Heilani (@heilannii) collaborated to create the "PASTEL GIRLS" photoshoot, which they state was directly inspired by the "I Choose You" music video; in August, Instagram tights and socks brand Tightsqueeze (@tiqhtsqueeze) began to take a more Candy Sleaze creative direction, releasing several polka dotted thigh-high socks in contrasting colorways (pink with blue lace trim, blue with yellow lace trim).
In the summer of 2026, American singer Justine Skye went on her CANDY Tour to promote her EP,
in which she often wore vibrant and revealing outfits on stage.
During the consideration of canonizing Candy Sleaze into the Aesthetics Wiki, it was decided to definitively divorce the aesthetic from its relation to Japanese fashion and

; this was done to curate the aesthetic into one identifiable trend, rather than allowing the term to be broadly applied to several similar, but ultimately unrelated, styles. Candy Sleaze is still influenced by and incorporates many instances of Asian media and fashion, but as a whole, is unrelated to J-fashion, and typically quite different from J-fashions' most common styling preferences and silhouettes.

The primary color combination in Candy Sleaze is blue, pink, and yellow. Turquoise and mint are the most popular shades of blue used, but any lighter shade of blue is common in the trend. These color choices lean into the "candy" idea of the aesthetic, and come off as eye-catching and feminine. These colors are often accented by inclusions of black or white, or sometimes even silver for a more futuristic,

Candy Sleaze outfits often utilize color blocking to make the contrast between the colors pop even more. Often, these blocked colors are plain, and paired with a patterned garment -- typically striped or polka dotted.

Other patterns that frequent the style are stars and checkerboards; common fashion motifs used are sequins, bows, hair clips, buttons, candy, and music- and tech-inspired designs (such as the MP3 player/iPod print skirt often seen, or garments with headphones or music notes printed on them).

Another common visual motif is bold, all-caps text printed on garments, particularly the word "swag," often stylized as "#SWAG," which is a callback to the Swag and Party Rock trends it draws inspiration from.

silhouette of Candy Sleaze is form-fitting
, with shirts sometimes being modified (tied or pinned back) to achieve this look. The trend is
overall quite revealing -- legs, midriff, and shoulders are often bare, and it is common to see panty lines ("whale tales") and bra cups showing

, or even as a main staple of the outfit. In some examples, the wearer is intentionally pants-less, with only underwear as a bottom; in other examples, the wearer will intentionally lift or crop their shirt to chest height in order to reveal their bra, or wear micro skirts/micro shorts. Since underwear is such a key feature of the look, it is worn with intention:
push-up bras, bikinis, thongs and g-strings, and underwear with patterns and colors that fit into the aesthetics' motifs
